facts.text: Hope was a juvenile female blue whale. She stranded on a sandbar at the mouth of Wexford Harbour, Ireland, on the morning of 25 March 1891.
The 4.5-tonne skeleton was sold to the Natural History Museum for £250.
The skeleton hung in the museum's Mammal Hall from 1934.
The skeleton was moved to Hintze Hall and unveiled there in July 2017.
In Hintze Hall she replaced the cast of Dippy the Diplodocus, which stood there from 1979 until January 2017.
She was named Hope "as a symbol of humanity's power to shape a sustainable future".

unsourced_facts.text: The skeleton has 221 bones and is posed in a diving lunge.

shots.narration: 抬头看。对，就是我。我叫“希望”，想给你讲个故事。
shots.action: A blue whale glides slowly through the air above the crowd and turns her head toward the viewer.

shots.narration: 很久以前，我是一头年幼的雌性蓝鲸，大海就是我的整个世界。
shots.action: The whale swims forward and does one slow barrel roll.

shots.narration: 1891年3月25日的清晨，我搁浅在一片沙洲上。
shots.action: The whale drifts into shallow water and comes to rest on a pale sandbar as small waves wash around her.

shots.narration: 那里是爱尔兰的韦克斯福德港口，远离我熟悉的深海。
shots.action: The whale lies still on the sandbar while the tide slowly pulls back around her.

shots.narration: 我的骨架重达四点五吨，被自然历史博物馆买下，只花了250英镑！
shots.action: The whale floats past and her body turns softly translucent, a glowing skeleton showing inside.

shots.narration: 从1934年起，我悬挂在哺乳动物展厅，静静地从高处望着人们。
shots.action: The whale hangs almost still high in the air while tiny visitors pass far below.

shots.narration: 2017年7月，我搬进辛兹大厅，接替了1979年起在此的梁龙“迪皮”。
shots.action: The whale sweeps down into the hall in one long diving lunge as visitors look up.

shots.narration: 我身长25.2米。这么大的身体，配得上一个大大的名字。
shots.action: The whale glides the full length of the hall, passing slowly over the camera from nose to tail.

shots.narration: 人们叫我“希望”，象征人类有力量塑造可持续的未来。 而这，要靠你们。
shots.action: The whale turns to face the viewer and glides gently closer.
